evaluationMethod: Master-resolution visual inspection against every mechanicalEvidence item, the revised dominant proof, familiar substitutions, iteration-1 defects, and whether downstream topology is legible without the prompt. Mechanical preflight was treated as evidence only, not an editorial gate.

results.title: River-width separation loom

mechanicalEvidence.observation: Multiple dark-green ribbons continue separately into the river with water corridors between them.
Large pale ceramic-ended drums carry the active ribbons; surfaces show dirt and water wear.

Two transverse white comb assemblies have open tops and raised hinged side arms, but only four thick teeth are visible on each, not five, and a third ribbon does not have its own equally legible comb.
No discrete clamps are legible along the visible ribbon edges.
A separate empty pale drum rests sideways on a wheeled foreground cart.
The replacement drum, active drums, deck, and standing water carry brown-gray staining and residue.
The separate drum is supported on a clearly wheeled steel service cart.
Wide open-water corridors remain between and beyond the membrane lanes.

revisedDominantProof.observation: Hinged ceramic comb language and the separate replacement drum are now dominant, but the required three five-tooth comb frames are not all present.

results.comparisonToIteration1: Clear improvement: iteration 1 lacked transverse comb frames and a separate replacement roll; iteration 2 supplies both, but undercounts and simplifies the comb assemblies and loses visible edge clamps.
results.rationale: The river-width loom, separate service drum, wet maintenance deck, independent lanes, and open navigation remain readable without the prompt. Mutate rather than pass because the dominant three-comb proof is incomplete and edge clamps are absent.

results.title: Library whose walls are the seasonal heat machine

mechanicalEvidence.observation: Readers, shelves, tables, and maintenance hardware occupy deep openings within a massive coursed mineral wall.

A long dark horizontal course opening exposes copper manifolds, but no complete removed cover is unmistakably leaning beside it; the projecting blocks read as structural masonry rather than a detached band.
Two sealed pale canisters stand on the cart and repeated fittings sit in the opening, but the specified row of matching ceramic cartridges is not clearly resolved.
A low four-caster cradle carries two pale sealed canisters in front of the maintenance opening.

mechanicalEvidence.item: shelves and seating inside thermal wall
mechanicalEvidence.observation: Book-filled shelving, reading tables, lamps, benches, and several ordinary readers occupy the deep alcoves.
Several deep wall alcoves are present, but a clearly deeper warmer refuge room through a very thick doorway is not distinct.
Mineral edges, tables, shelving, and floor surfaces show scuffing and accumulated wear.

revisedDominantProof.observation: Occupied library alcoves are unequivocal, but the removed structural course-joint cover is not visibly detached and leaning beside the exposed opening.

results.comparisonToIteration1: Strong improvement in library legibility: books, readers, tables, and lamps replace iteration 1's nearly empty porous wall. The maintenance band remains unresolved, and the cartridge row is less explicit than iteration 1's clear wheeled rack.
results.rationale: The inhabited thermal-wall library and public maintenance access survive, so the scene is not a generic conventional library. It cannot pass because the revised removed-band proof and deeper refuge chamber remain ambiguous.

results.title: Quarry-scale continuous fabricator

mechanicalEvidence.observation: A black rail-and-carriage system runs from the lower foreground to the distant quarry horizon.
No two distinct downward nozzles can be identified actively laying the dark and pale strata.
Dark wet and pale porous deposited banks differ visibly in material and surface moisture.
The deposited banks widen, narrow, turn, and change height across the quarry bed.
A clear Y-shaped channel junction splits around the central carriage.
Two enormous ribbed spools dominate the lower foreground carriage.
Carriage structure and narrow gantry access are visible, but a distinct guardrailed maintenance platform is not prominent.
No rough rectangular repair splice with clamp scars interrupts the otherwise continuous deposited strata.

revisedDominantProof.observation: Foreground reinforcement spools and the Y-junction are dominant, but the repaired deposition interruption is missing.

results.comparisonToIteration1: Clear improvement: iteration 2 adds dominant reinforcement spools and an unmistakable Y-junction. It regresses on visible two-nozzle deposition and still omits the repaired interruption required to prove maintenance of continuous strata.
results.rationale: The quarry-scale continuous branching fabrication territory is readable without the prompt and avoids a house-printer or giant robot-arm substitution. Mutation is required because active deposition and its repaired failure mode are not legible.

results.title: Freight body repaired like a textile

mechanicalEvidence.observation: A long black underframe supports the tension table, but a separate aligned freight vehicle frame behind the table is not clearly distinguishable.
The stretched sheet has a broad pale abraded center strip, not a precise opened diagonal seam.
A broad waist-high black table dominates almost the entire room and supports the stretched skin.
Repeated thick accordion-like pleats sit on a wheeled cradle along the right side, though the folds are unusually tube-like.
Long copper-colored pins repeat along both edges of the stretched skin.
Repeated dark clamp bodies connect the copper pins to the sheet edges and pull radially outward.
A large pale scuffed and abraded strip runs along the skin.
The pinned edges read as an active tension operation, but no clearly half-installed replacement seam is visible.

revisedDominantProof.observation: The tension table and wheeled accordion replacement skin now dominate the frame, correcting the primary iteration-1 omission.

results.comparisonToIteration1: Major improvement: iteration 1 showed skins hanging from a frame with no table or folded replacement; iteration 2 makes the infrastructural textile floor unmistakable. It loses the diagonal opened seam and separates the freight frame poorly from the table structure.
results.rationale: The room now reads as large-scale textile repair rather than simple panel hanging. It remains a mutation because the vehicle frame, opened diagonal seam, and half-completed repinning operation are not sufficiently explicit.

results.title: Underground winter daylight room

mechanicalEvidence.observation: Several thick luminous bands turn from walls into the ceiling, but they are broad panel-like strips separated by concrete rather than clearly solid opaque-sided ceramic ribs.
The luminous bands visibly turn through approximately ninety degrees from wall to ceiling.
Minor brightness variation exists, but most luminous bands share the same warm glow.
No rib contains a dark rectangular service gap.
No dark gasket joints bound a removed segment.
The room has a wall recess and public floor, not a distinct side maintenance gallery.
Two glowing rectangular blocks sit on wheeled carts, but they do not match the long curved rib geometry and read as luminous furniture or material samples.
Communal tables, chairs, cups, and floor surfaces show ordinary use and wear.

revisedDominantProof.observation: The dark removed-segment gap, matching replacement segment, and side gallery are absent; luminous broad ceiling bands still dominate over opaque load-bearing ribs.

results.substitutedTypology: architectural luminous ceiling bands / skylight-like light wells
results.comparisonToIteration1: The darker opaque vault and heavier supports improve weight and enclosure over iteration 1's translucent canopy, but the image still substitutes continuous luminous ceiling panels and again omits the service gap, gaskets, gallery, and matching segment. The two glowing cart blocks do not prove segment replacement.
results.rationale: Reject: without the prompt this reads as an underground communal room with luminous architectural ceiling bands, not maintainable solid light-guide ribs. The required repair topology and downstream service gallery are absent.
